correctness.rationale: Exact normalized path cosine eigenbasis and positive endpoint coordinates give Vandermonde squared Gram determinant. Its half-logarithmic second derivative is strictly negative; first derivative moves from +infinity to -sum_{i<j}lambda_i, strictly negative only for m>=3; m=2 remains positive. Exact rescaled eigenvalue identity r_j=rho_{(m-1)/(N-1)}(j/(m-1)), compact-uniform cosine profile convergence, uniform triangular Riemann sums and monotone root bracketing rigorously yield all theta limits including theta=0 and 1. I independently computed the N=13,m=7 root and verified the direct determinant derivative. The finite test does not prove the asymptotic theorem.

value.rationale: The full bandwidth crossover is a natural design invariant for endpoint heat observation of path graph low-frequency signals, resolving a previously fixed sampling interval in adjacent literature. Distinguishes an exceptional m=2 boundary, identifies unique optimal timing for every m>=3, and gives a sharp diffusive scaling; this is more than a standard rank criterion or trivial substitution.

final_claim: For N>=3 and 3<=m<=N, endpoint m-sample normalized-path heat D-optimal uniform spacing exists and is unique (m=2 no finite maximizer). With m->infinity and m/N->theta in [0,1], tau*lambda_(m-1) tends to the unique double-integral root s_theta; the low-bandwidth coefficient is 2s_0/pi^2 and full-band limit s_1/2.
